info.title: tasmota-power
info.description: Multi-driver smart plug control and energy monitoring per printer (Tasmota, Shelly Gen1/Gen2+, Zigbee2MQTT, ESPHome, OpenBeken, Generic MQTT, and Home Assistant).

get.summary: Get the connection settings and their live state
get.description: Returns the MQTT broker and Home Assistant settings with secrets left out, whether each connection is up, the state of the built-in broker and whether its port is granted, and which values are pinned by the host's own settings. The host takes view_resource on the module before this is called.

200.description: Current MQTT settings and broker status

put.description: Replaces the whole settings object in settings.json and reconnects the MQTT broker. A value pinned in the host's own settings is kept as pinned. The host takes view_resource on the module before this is called, and the module asks the host whether the caller holds configure_resource. A caller who does not is refused with FORBIDDEN (403).

200.description: Updated MQTT settings and broker status

post.description: Tests connecting to the provided (or saved) external or built-in MQTT broker settings and returns whether the connection succeeded or the exact error. The built-in broker is tested on the port the operator granted. The host takes view_resource on the module before this is called, and the module asks the host whether the caller holds configure_resource. A caller who does not is refused with FORBIDDEN (403).

post.summary: Test Home Assistant REST connectivity and list switch/power entities
post.description: Tests connecting to the provided (or saved) Home Assistant URL and Long-Lived Access Token via GET /api/ and returns discovered switch, input_boolean, and power sensor entities. The host takes view_resource on the module before this is called, and the module asks the host whether the caller holds configure_resource. A caller who does not is refused with FORBIDDEN (403).

200.description: Home Assistant test result and entity list

post.summary: Ask the MQTT broker which plugs are there
post.description: Queries the broker for Tasmota and Shelly Gen1 plugs and returns every plug found. The host takes view_resource on the module before this is called, and the module asks the host whether the caller holds configure_resource. A caller who does not is refused with FORBIDDEN (403).

get.summary: List every printer's plug and the plugs the broker found
get.description: Returns each printer's saved plug, the plugs the broker found, the Home Assistant entities, and the state of both connections. The host takes view_resource on the module before this is called, and the module asks the host whether the caller holds configure_resource. A caller who does not is refused with FORBIDDEN (403).

200.description: All printer plug assignments and discovered plugs

get.summary: List every printer's plug and what it draws now
get.description: Returns, for every printer the caller may see that has a plug or an auto-off choice, the saved plug with secrets left out, its live state and readings, and the energy since it was turned on. It reads memory only, so one request serves a whole list of printers. can_configure and each printer's can_operate say what the caller may change, for what a page offers; each answer is kept for 30 seconds, and the routes ask again. The host takes view_resource on the module before this is called.

200.description: Every visible printer's plug, and the state of both connections

parameters.name: history
parameters.description: Minutes of power samples each printer carries, for a graph: 1 to 60, larger values are read as 60. Without it, no samples.

get.summary: Get one printer's plug, its live state, its power graph and its safety lock
get.description: Returns the printer's saved plug, live relay and power readings, rolling power graph samples, session and per-print energy totals, the active-print safety lock, and the auto-off countdown. The host takes view_resource on the module before this is called.

200.description: Device power plug status and energy usage telemetry

put.summary: Save one printer's plug and its auto-off choices
put.description: Saves the driver, the plug's address (an MQTT topic, an IP address or host, a Home Assistant entity, or custom MQTT topics), the relay, the auto-off-after-print flag, and an optional delay of the printer's own. Answers 409 when another printer already has that plug and relay. The host takes view_resource on the module before this is called, and the module asks the host whether the caller holds configure_resource, and operate on the printer. A caller who does not is refused with FORBIDDEN (403).

post.summary: Turn a printer's plug on or off
post.description: Switches the plug through its driver and verifies the resulting state. Refuses OFF, and a TOGGLE that would turn off, with 409 Conflict while the printer is printing or busy. The host takes view_resource on the module before this is called, and the module asks the host whether the caller holds operate_resource and operate on the printer. A caller who does not is refused with FORBIDDEN (403).

200.description: Command sent and updated plug status

post.summary: Choose whether a printer turns off after a print
post.description: With enabled alone, arms or disarms turning off after the print that runs now or the next one; the printer then goes back to its default. With default as well, sets whether the printer turns off after every print. The host takes view_resource on the module before this is called, and the module asks the host whether the caller holds operate_resource and operate on the printer. A caller who does not is refused with FORBIDDEN (403).

config.description: The saved plug, with secrets left out

plug.description: The live state and readings of the plug, absent for a printer with no plug

power_history.description: The power samples of the minutes ?history= asks for. An empty list when asked and there are none; absent when not asked.

can_operate.description: Whether the caller may switch this printer's plug.

can_configure.description: Whether the caller may change plugs and connections.

Refusal.description: One refusal, as RFC 9457 names it.

status.description: The HTTP status, repeated in the body.

code.description: The fault code: ROUTE_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_INPUT, NOT_CONFIGURED, PRINTER_BUSY, BROKER_OFFLINE, PLUG_REFUSED, TOPIC_ALREADY_ASSIGNED, NO_PRINCIPAL, FORBIDDEN, ACCESS_UNKNOWN, CHECKS_NOT_APPROVED or INTERNAL_ERROR, in this module's fault domain.

Refused.description: The module refused the call. The code says which rule it met.
